title: the DSG mining excavation veins and shoring

banner.title: The DSG MINING EXCAVATION, VEINS AND SHORING, R520: printed pp. 49-50 (pdf 50-51) - the excavation rules (the hard and slow necessity of tunneling, the Table 27 rates grid reprinted from DMG page 106 in cubic feet per miner per eight hours across very soft, soft and hard rock - the eight races from gnoll/halfling/human 75/50/25 through gnome/kobold 80/60/30, goblin/orc 85/65/30, dwarf/hobgoblin 90/70/35, ogre 150/100/50, hill giant 250/150/75 and fire/frost giant 300/200/100 to stone giant 500/350/175), the per-race 10-foot-tunnel miner maxima (the small races 16, man-sized 12, gnoll 8, ogre 6, giant 4), the vein rules (the 10x10 tunnel following the shifting vein, the 1d6 x 10-feet depth to intersect the vein, the 1d4 direction roll on Table 28 - north-south, east-west, northeast-southwest, northwest-southeast - the at-least-20-feet run, the secret 1d8 alteration roll per 20-foot section on Table 29 - steep descent, shallow descent, curves right and left at 10-60 degrees, the 5-6 continues straight, shallow ascent, steep ascent - the must-follow rule, the impossible-course run-out with the other-direction freedom, the both-ends stop taking priority over the Duration of A Mining Site rules, and the gorge pickup at DM discretion), and the shoring rules (the wooden or stone support pillars against the almost-certain cave-in, the carpenter, stonemason and miner proficiencies, the two side braces plus a ceiling brace per 10-foot section, the 30 feet of at-least-one-foot-diameter bracing in the standard 10x10 tunnel, the four man-hours per set, and the 18/50-strength solo-moving threshold with the manpower or animal alternative)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~6465-6560) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 67 = printed p. 50) and the compiled-tables appendix reprint as the third read - every numeric cell multi-confirmed: the Table 27 grid (chapter djvu clean, the Capture window corroborating 90/70/35, 150/100/50 and 250/150/75, the appendix reprint corroborating 75/50, 80/60, 85/65, 90/70 and the ogre/hill giant rows; the fire/frost 300/200/100 and stone giant 500/350/175 rows read from the clean chapter djvu against the DMG page 106 reprint origin), the miner maxima 16/12/8/6/4 (chapter + Capture agree), the 1d6 x 10-feet vein depth, the 1d4 direction, the 20-foot sections, and the shoring numbers 2/1/30/1/4 man-hours with the 18/50 threshold. THE DJVU D6 GARBLE: the Table 29 header reads D6 Roll but lists eight results; both the chapter and the appendix reprint list the same eight rows and the secret roll is 1d8 - settled as a d8 table with the 5-6 band as one row. The DMG page 106 seam, the DSG page 53 duration seam and the R511 cave-in seam are noted. The Products of a Mine grids (Tables 30-32) start the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: Three tables pin: Table 27 as an 8x3 rates grid (very soft, soft, hard), Table 28 as a 4x2 d4 direction grid (each direction a single face, lo = hi), and Table 29 as a 7x2 d8 band grid (the 5-6 continues-straight band pinning as one row per the R518 pin-as-printed lesson). The vein depth pins as dice + sides consts with the 10-feet multiplier separate per the R508 convention; the 1d8 alteration roll pins the same way with the D6-header garble settled by the appendix reprint. The 18/50 strength threshold pins as a prose bool, not a computed comparison. The DMG 106, DSG 53 and R511 seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.

Wisdom-score find chance plus the miner proficiency
modifier, the no-yield regions of deep sand/dirt and

split, strip mining excluded (heavy equipment), the
shallow-pan placer sifting of eroded streambed wealth

dealing primarily with tunnel mining. Numbers dual-read on

consts.name: dnfT27RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 27 mining rates grid carries eight races of miner.

consts.name: dnfT28RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 28 vein direction grid carries the four d4 directions.

consts.name: dnfT29RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 29 vein path alterations grid carries seven bands over the eight d8 results (the 5-6 continues-straight band is one row).

consts.name: dnfMaxMinersSmall
consts.comment: the maximum number of miners that can work in a 10-foot-wide tunnel: dwarf, gnome, goblin, halfling and kobold 16.

consts.name: dnfMaxMinersMan
consts.comment: hobgoblin, human and orc 12.

consts.name: dnfMaxMinersGnoll
consts.comment: gnoll 8.

consts.name: dnfMaxMinersOgre
consts.comment: ogre 6.

consts.name: dnfMaxMinersGiant
consts.comment: giant (any) 4.

consts.name: dnfTunnelWidthFt
consts.comment: a mine tunnel path typically requires a 10-foot-wide tunnel.

consts.name: dnfTunnelHeightFt
consts.comment: the typical 10-foot-wide by 10-foot-high tunnel.

consts.name: dnfVeinDepthDice
consts.comment: when a miner first discovers a mineral vein, roll 1d6; the tunnel must be dug down to intersect the vein.

consts.name: dnfVeinDepthSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d6 vein-depth roll, pinned as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention.

consts.name: dnfVeinDepthMultFt
consts.comment: multiply the 1d6 result by 10; this is how far down (in feet) the tunnel must be dug to intersect the mineral vein.

consts.name: dnfVeinSectionFt
consts.comment: the vein always runs at least 20 feet in the direction indicated; after each 20-foot section of tunnel is excavated the DM secretly rolls 1d8 for the path.

consts.name: dnfVeinAlterationDice
consts.comment: the secret per-section vein alteration roll is 1d8, read on Table 29.

consts.name: dnfVeinAlterationSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d8 alteration roll (the djvu table header garbles D6; both the chapter and the appendix reprint list eight rows, settled as D8).

consts.name: dnfShoringSideBraces
consts.comment: each 10-foot section of tunnel requires two side braces and a ceiling brace.

consts.name: dnfShoringCeilingBraces
consts.comment: the single ceiling brace of each shoring set.

consts.name: dnfShoringBracingFt
consts.comment: in the standard 10-wide by 10-high tunnel the shoring set takes 30 feet of bracing that is at least one foot in diameter.

consts.name: dnfShoringDiameterFt
consts.comment: the minimum one-foot diameter of the shoring braces.

consts.name: dnfShoringManHours
consts.comment: each set of shoring supports takes four man-hours to construct.

bools.name: dnfRatesReprintedFromDmg106
bools.comment: the Table 27 excavation rates are reprinted from page 106 of the DMG (the cross-book seam).

bools.name: dnfRatesPerMinerPerEightHours
bools.comment: the excavation rates are given in cubic feet per miner per eight-hour period.

bools.name: dnfExcavatingHardAndSlow
bools.comment: excavating a tunnel is hard and time-consuming, but is necessary to remove the mineral wealth of the underdark.

bools.name: dnfMaxMinersDependsOnRace
bools.comment: the maximum number of miners that can work in a 10-foot-wide tunnel depends on race.

bools.name: dnfTunnelFollowsShiftingVein
bools.comment: a mine tunnel must follow the shifting vein of a mineral through the earth.

bools.name: dnfDirectionRollIsD4
bools.comment: once the vein is discovered, to determine the path of the vein roll 1d4, with the result indicating the direction on Table 28.

bools.name: dnfVeinRunsAtLeastSection
bools.comment: the vein always runs at least 20 feet in the indicated direction before the next secret alteration roll.

bools.name: dnfAlterationRollIsSecret
bools.comment: the 1d8 alteration roll is made secretly by the DM after each 20-foot section.

bools.name: dnfMustFollowUnwantedDirection
bools.comment: miners who wish to continue working the mine must follow the vein, even if it goes in a direction they would rather not follow.

bools.name: dnfImpossibleCourseRunsOut
bools.comment: if the vein path becomes impossible to follow, such as emerging into thin air through a sheer cliff face, that course of the mine has run out - though the miners are free to follow the vein in the other direction.

bools.name: dnfBothEndsStopsMine
bools.comment: if both directions of a vein end, the mine provides no more minerals; this rule takes priority over the Duration of A Mining Site rules (the DSG page 53 seam).

bools.name: dnfGorgePickupAtDiscretion
bools.comment: in unusual circumstances, such as a vein ending in a cliff with a facing cliff across a narrow gorge, characters may attempt to pick up the vein again across the gorge; the success is left to the DM’s discretion, generally a determined probability and a die roll.

bools.name: dnfShoringOrCaveIn
bools.comment: a tunnel mine must be regularly protected with wooden or stone support pillars, called shoring, or else sections of the tunnel will almost certainly cave in (the R511 cave-in seam).

bools.name: dnfShoringProficiencies
bools.comment: shoring can be accomplished by characters with carpenter, stonemason, or miner proficiencies.

bools.name: dnfStrongSoloMoving
bools.comment: unless the character doing the shoring is extremely strong (18/50 or greater strength), moving the braces into the mine requires additional manpower or animal help.
